findings.desc: clobber-safety miss: parsePorcelainDirtyPaths incorrectly decodes git-quoted non-ASCII paths. unquoteGitPath uses JSON.parse which throws on git octal escapes (e.g. \303\251 for é), then falls back to path.slice(1,-1) leaving literal backslash-octal in the string. normalizeGitPath then replaces those backslashes with forward slashes, producing a corrupted path like src/caf/303/251.ts instead of src/café.ts. The affected set from listDoneMergeAffectedPaths uses -z (NUL-separated, never quoted) so it carries raw UTF-8 bytes. The two forms never match, so a dirty non-ASCII-named file that is IN the merge affected set is not detected as overlapping, and the DONE merge proceeds when it should be blocked — silent clobber of uncommitted work on that file.
